title: Toward Understanding Bias Correlations for Mitigation in NLP
base_benchmarks: Jigsaw Unintended Bias in Toxicity Classification
findings: In toxicity detection, religious bias was found to be positively correlated with gender and racial biases, meaning that debiasing for one identity could help reduce bias for others. However, in word embeddings, biases showed negative correlations, where sequentially debiasing for one identity (e.g., gender) could be less effective or even detrimental to debiasing for another identity (e.g., religion). In both tasks, a joint debiasing approach that mitigates all biases simultaneously was found to be more effective at reducing total bias, including religious bias, than independent or sequential debiasing methods.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured unintended bias in toxicity detection models against religious identity terms (Christian, Jewish, Muslim). The analysis focused on how a model's bias against one identity (e.g., gender) correlates with its bias against religious identities.
